:::{#sol-subspace-practice}

No.
The vector $\tp{(0, 1)}$ is in $\mathcal{H}$,
but $(-1) \cd \tp{(0, 1)} = \tp{(0, -1)}$ is not,
because its second entry is negative.
So $\mathcal{H}$ fails condition 2 of @def-subspace,
and it is not a [subspace](#def-subspace).
$\mathcal{H}$ does satisfy condition 1,
which shows that one condition alone is not enough.

:::
